messages:
maya: quick heads-up — after merging Asteria's LoRA into the int8 variant we ship, the quick eval pack flags a weird invoice-amount hallucination. small sample below.

maya: eval summary (100 prompts, billing subset):
```
baseline (fp16, adapter-off): amount-err-rate=0.9%
loRA+fp16: amount-err-rate=1.1%
loRA+int8 (gptq): amount-err-rate=6.8%  <-- regression
most failures: swapped digits or extra zeros (e.g., expected 132.50 -> got 312.50 or 13250)
```

jordan: ouch. any deterministic repro? can you paste one input/output pair? :thinking:

maya: yep — one example from the pack:
```
INPUT: "Invoice lines: item A $40.00, item B $92.50. What is the total amount?"
EXPECTED: "$132.50"
MODEL (loRA+int8): "$312.50"
```

noah: interesting — looks like digit transposition, could be tokenization shift or quantization-induced logits bias. did tokenizer mapping change between variants?

maya: tokenizer same. adapter merge changes only weights. but int8 kernel & rounding might amplify small probs. ops-runner ran int8 job with `quant_group=128` and `use_fastmath=true`.

ops-runner: deploy log snippet:
```
model: asteria-lora-v3
quant: gptq-int8
batch-size: 8
kv-cache: enabled
config: quant_group=128,use_fastmath=true
run_id: r-20241123-03
```

noah: can you repro with `use_fastmath=false` and a smaller quant_group (64)? also try disabling KV cache to rule out alignment bug.

maya: will run. launching 3 quick jobs: int8-fastmath-on (baseline), int8-fastmath-off, int8-q64. kicking off with eval-bot.

eval-bot: scheduled evals: 1) int8-fastmath-on (r-1001) 2) int8-fastmath-off (r-1002) 3) int8-q64 (r-1003). each will run the 100-example billing pack and upload CSV. ETA ~ 12m.

sophia: also try a tiny FP16 run with the same LoRA weights (no quant) — that isolates quantization vs merge problem.

maya: good call. added fp16-lora (r-1004).

(eval-bot sends quick update)
eval-bot: r-1002 done (int8-fastmath-off): amount-err-rate=2.0% — big improvement but still above baseline. failures mainly truncated/extra-zero errors. CSV: https://internal.redwood/evals/r-1002.csv

jordan: ok that points to fastmath being a multiplier but not sole cause. can we diff logits for a failing step between fp16 and int8 to see token-level probs?

ops-runner: can pull per-token logits for a sample. attaching tiny snippet (fp16 vs int8):
```
step 34 token: "$"
fp16_p: 0.84
int8_p: 0.72
next_token (fp16): "1" (p=0.62)
next_token (int8): "3" (p=0.58)
```

noah: that's telling — probabilities shifted for numeric digits, switching the top token. quant noise nudged the argmax. two mitigations: 1) post-process numeric canonicalization (parse & reformat), 2) calibration/fine-grain quant (q64) or mixed-precision critical layers.

maya: customer (Asteria) is sensitive to numeric accuracy. they asked for a patch within the week. proposing short-term: deploy post-process that extracts numbers and recomputes totals when prompt looks like an invoice. medium-term: re-run quant with q64 and attempt mixed-precision on numeric head.

sophia: agreed. post-process as guardrail is low-risk. i'll draft the canonicalization rules: strip chars, parse floats, if model output differs by >$1, prefer computed sum and flag for audit.

jordan: also recommend adding a small numeric-focused augment to the eval pack (more edge cases: leading zeros, commas, currency symbols, negative adjustments). we should run that nightly against all quant variants.

maya: adding augment now. will follow up with final recommendation after r-1003 and r-1004 complete. thanks all. :thumbsup:

(eval-bot later)
eval-bot: r-1003 (int8-q64) done: amount-err-rate=1.2% — nearly FP16. r-1004 (fp16-lora) done: amount-err-rate=1.0%

maya: final take: int8-q64 mostly recovers behavior; fastmath caused most error amplification. immediate plan: 1) deploy invoice post-process for Asteria (short-term) 2) enable int8-q64 for Asteria model in prod (medium-term) 3) follow-up: test mixed-precision on numeric-sensitive head and add numeric augment to nightly evals.

noah: sounds good. please open a rollout PR with config changes and link the audit CSVs.

maya: will do — PR + changelog after lunch.
